top_categories.workout_context: 13,878ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Road-specific control matters at Maratona dles Dolomites. Practice on alpine mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 85 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Maratona dles Dolomites' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
162ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Maratona dles Dolomites, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
13,878ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Maratona dles Dolomites. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Maratona dles Dolomites. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
At mile 60 of 85, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on alpine mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 85 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,878ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: July in La Villa → Corvara, Alta Badia, South Tyrol — Valley 20-28°C, summits 8-15°C lower. Dawn start potentially single digits. 63% rain chance. Thunderstorm risk HIGH — afternoon storms common. Mandatory rain jacket enforced (no vests). Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Maratona dles Dolomites. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Maratona dles Dolomites’s 85 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Maratona dles Dolomites reaches approximately 7,400ft above sea level. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Summits above 2,200m can feel near-freezing in rain.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Maratona dles Dolomites demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride alpine mountain passes at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 85 miles of alpine mountain passes in La Villa → Corvara, Alta Badia, South Tyrol.
